# Statistical Modeling and Machine Learning

Student presentations in this chapter concern statistical reasoning,
prediction, dimension reduction, clustering, and supervised learning.

| Presentation | Presenter | Description |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [Decision Trees](../topic/decision-trees/) | Mahiba Mansur | Classification. |
| [Perfect Separation in Logistic Regression](../topic/morissette-separation/) | Carter Morissette | Limits of logistic regression. |
| [Random Forest](../topic/sadie-bucco-random-forest/) | Sadie Bucco | Ensemble Classification. |
The decision-tree presentation fits a small classifier using request fields
available at creation, compares it with a majority baseline, and explains
why accuracy alone can hide missed Illegal Parking requests.

The perfect-separation presentation simulates a pass/fail example where one
cutoff splits the outcomes perfectly, so logistic regression has no finite
best slope. It shows the warning signs, then compares a ridge penalty and
merged categories as fixes and previews Firth's method.

The decision tree presentation introduces random forest and explains how it
improves on single decision trees through bootstrapping and feature
subsampling. It walks through a classification example in Python using NYC 311
Service Request data, covering evaluation metrics and grid search tuning, and
closes with the method's key limitations.
